- **self**: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor (6/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Artificial Hivemind (NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks oral) documents mode collapse in open-ended generation on 26K real-world queries: intra-model repetition and, more strongly, inter-model homogeneity, where different models produce strikingly similar outputs. This is the general mechanism that would make the same vehicle domains recur across vendors. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954 · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.04732

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Even when told to avoid metaphor, 6.27% of ChatGPT's text stayed metaphorical, and its metaphor identification differed significantly from a human linguist's: metaphor is used rhetorically without tracking conceptual boundaries, which is the condition under which mixed or ill-fitting source domains slip through. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739 · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The same study found source-domain variety rose for abstract targets (Politics used 21 distinct source domains), so collapse is topic-dependent rather than uniform. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739 · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor
- [statement] A 2026 computational audit (Chang, Qu, Li, arXiv 2604.04732) reports 'representational collapse': LLMs flatten culturally distinct metaphorical framings, with some prompts (e.g. metaphors for Death under India and China personas) yielding compact clusters that reuse essentially one metaphor; a cultural persona sometimes narrows rather than widens the metaphor space. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.04732 · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor
- [statement] LLM-generated metaphor norms track word-co-occurrence properties (familiarity, metaphoricity) well but track aptness and concreteness, which need topic-vehicle reasoning, only weakly to moderately. That fits vehicle choice driven by frequency rather than fit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/language-sciences/articles/10.3389/flang.2026.1756514/xml · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor

## Facts and statements

- [statement] In a 20-speech ChatGPT corpus (10 topics, MIPVU-coded), the model heavily favoured the Planting source domain across Education, Economy and Health (e.g. 'sowing seeds of growth', 'cultivating knowledge'): one vehicle domain reused across unrelated targets. (low confidence) — https://lacuna.tiptreesystems.com/work/corpus-driven-analysis-of-conceptual-metaphor-in-artificial-intelligence/wrk_79c3cb6959455c94b969a0ba9f71f739 · keywords: Source-domain collapse in LLM metaphor
